evidence.summary: books table: id integer primary key, title text not null, author text.
GET /api/books returns a JSON array of {id, title, author} for every book (no paging, no filter, no owner).
ratings table: book_id integer references books(id), stars integer with CHECK (stars between 1 and 5); no primary key and no uniqueness, so a book can collect many ratings.
PUT /api/books/{id}/rating reads JSON field 'stars', returns 400 {error: 'stars must be 1 to 5'} outside 1-5, otherwise inserts a new ratings row (append, not update) and returns {ok: true}.
GET /api/books/export returns JSON (code comment says 'JSON, not CSV') of {title, stars} from books left join ratings: one row per rating, a book with no rating gets stars null.
Data is stored in SQLite through Python's sqlite3; file path from SHELFIE_DB, default shelfie.db.
SHELFIE_SESSION_SECRET is read at startup and is required (the process fails if it is unset) but is never used anywhere else in the code; it is not mentioned in any doc.
One Python process: a single BaseHTTPRequestHandler served by http.server.HTTPServer on port 8080 handles every route; no separate services, no gateway.
No handler checks a session, token or user; every route is open. No DB.commit() call exists, so inserted ratings are never committed.
Quoted claim: export the library as CSV at GET /api/v1/books/export.csv. Contradicted by the code (A-E05: JSON at /api/books/export).
Quoted claim: rate books from 1 to 10. Contradicted by the code (A-E03, A-E04: 1 to 5, enforced in handler and database).
Quoted claim: stores data in PostgreSQL. Contradicted by the code (A-E06: SQLite).
Claims three services (catalog, ratings, gateway for auth and routing), each with its own database. Contradicted by the code (A-E08 single process, one SQLite file; A-E09 no auth).
Spec lists GET /api/v1/books, GET /api/v1/books/export.csv and PUT /api/v1/books/{id}/rating with field 'score' integer 1-10. Code serves /api/books, /api/books/export and field 'stars' 1-5 instead.

An unknown GET path falls through without sending any response; a non-integer book id or stars value raises an unhandled exception; no check that the book exists (SQLite does not enforce the foreign key by default).

architecture.backend: single-process monolith: one http.server handler class and one SQLite connection (the docs' three-service design is not what the code does)

features.name: Browse the library
features.description: List every book in the library with its title and author.
features.observed_behaviour: GET /api/books returns a JSON array of {id, title, author}. There is no endpoint to add, edit or delete books.
features.business_logic: title is required (not null); author optional. No owner: one shared library.
features.integration: Needs one Book entity; in a multi-user app books need an owner.

features.name: Rate a book (1-5 stars)
features.description: Give a book a star rating from 1 to 5.
features.observed_behaviour: PUT /api/books/{id}/rating with JSON {stars}; 400 if outside 1-5; otherwise appends a new ratings row. Docs claim a 1-10 'score' at /api/v1, which the code does not do.
features.business_logic: stars integer 1..5, checked in the handler and by a database CHECK constraint; every PUT appends (no single current rating per book).
features.integration: Needs Book; unified app needs one rating per user per book.

features.name: Export the library (JSON)
features.description: Download the library's titles with their ratings as JSON.
features.observed_behaviour: GET /api/books/export returns JSON [{title, stars}] from a left join, so a book appears once per rating, or once with stars null. Docs claim CSV at /api/v1/books/export.csv, which the code does not serve.
features.business_logic: No format negotiation; author and id are not included.
features.integration: Reads Book and Rating; in a multi-user app it must export only the caller's library.

auth.session: none (SHELFIE_SESSION_SECRET is required at startup but unused)

configuration.purpose: Required at startup, never used; not documented. Probably meant for sessions that were never built (inferred).

error_handling.behaviour: no response is sent at all

error_handling.case: non-integer id or stars, missing body
error_handling.behaviour: unhandled exception; the client gets no proper error response

error_handling.case: rating a book that does not exist
error_handling.behaviour: accepted; foreign keys are not enforced by SQLite by default
no commit is ever made, so ratings written through the API are lost when the process exits (inferred from Python sqlite3 transaction behaviour; not run)
